proof:
The endpoint triangles have vertex lists $(-7/30,-13/30),(2/3,-7/30),(-13/30,2/3)$ and $(-13/30,-7/30),(2/3,-13/30),(-7/30,2/3)$. Summing their vertices pairwise and taking the hull of the averages gives $D$ with these counterclockwise vertices
$$
(-13/30,13/60),\ (-1/3,-1/3),\ (13/60,-13/30),\
(2/3,-1/3),\ (13/60,13/60),\ (-1/3,2/3).
$$
Each listed point is a pairwise average and the other three averages lie in this polygon, as seen by its six edge halfspaces. At the middle base every representation combines an average of the endpoint fibers with a point of $D$, or uses only $D$. This proves exact realization. The endpoint determinants and the shoelace formula for $D$ give $w=103/200$ and $W=13/20$. The three caps cover because their margins sum to zero. Every vertex of $K$ is in $D$ and strictly satisfies just its own one of the three margins, establishing essentiality.

The determinant-one map $(x,y)\mapsto(-x-y,x)$ permutes the vertices of $K$, commutes with $J$, and cyclically permutes the cap margins. Hence each body has a common fraction for all three caps. The $x$-positive cap in $A$ retains one vertex with positive coordinate $2/3$. On the two incident edges the respective clipping ratios from that vertex are $(2/3)/(9/10)$ and $(2/3)/(11/10)$, giving fraction $f=400/891$. In $B$ the denominators interchange. In $D$, intersecting with $x\ge0$ yields the five vertices $(0,-13/33),(13/60,-13/30),(2/3,-1/3),(13/60,13/60),(0,13/33)$. Their area by the shoelace formula is $299/990$, so $f_0=46/99$ and $f_0-f=14/891>0$. Thus the common mass is $2wf+Wf_0=6811/8910$, and division by $M$ gives the stated fraction.

Write $p=(r_-+r_+)/2$ and $q=(r_--r_+)/2$. Actual compatibility requires $(r_-A+r_+B)/2\subseteq r_0D$. In direction $(1,-1)$ the supports of $A,B$ are $9/10,11/10$, and in direction $(2,1)$ they are $11/10,9/10$. In both directions $h_D=1$. The two support inequalities give $r_0\ge p+|q|/10$. Dilation about zero preserves each through-origin cap fraction. Therefore the new total mass and common cap mass are
$$
M'=2w(p^2+q^2)+Wr_0^2,\qquad C'=fM'+W(f_0-f)r_0^2.
$$
The conditions $M'\ge M$ and $C'\le fM+W(f_0-f)$ imply $9/10<r_0\le1$. Since $0<p\le r_0-|q|/10$, expansion gives
$$
M'\le Mr_0^2-(2w/5)r_0|q|+(101w/50)q^2.
$$
For $0<|q|<1/10$ the last two terms are at most $-(79/500)w|q|<0$, contradicting $M'\ge M$. If $q=0$, equality in the mass bound forces $p=r_0=1$.

For the first-order statement put $r_i=(1+t\sigma_i)^{1/2}$. In the support direction $(1,0)$ both endpoint supports and the middle support equal $2/3$, so the active support gap has derivative $a\cdot\sigma/2$. The cap derivative is $c\cdot\sigma$, and the total derivative is $(w,W,w)\cdot\sigma$. Substitution of $w,W,f,f_0$ gives the displayed row identity. Its cap coefficient is positive, so fixed mass and cap nonincrease imply $a\cdot\sigma\le0$.

Finally the threefold rotation fixes only the continuous origin, so all fiber centroids are there. Every containing closed ambient halfspace at $(0,0)$ contains the middle centroid and at least one endpoint centroid, as its base margin at the two endpoints is affine. For each such positive fiber apply accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d with its full area, which gives the fraction $\Gamma_2=4/9$ at its centroid. Pure-base traces contain the whole corresponding fibers. Therefore the normalized depth is at least $\Gamma_2(W+w)/M=233/756$.

statement:
Let $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1/3,-1/3),(2/3,-1/3),(-1/3,2/3)\}$, $J=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&-2\\2&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, $A=(I+J/10)K$, $B=(I-J/10)K$, and $D=(A+B)/2$. At bases $-1,0,1$ use $A,D,B$ as the integer fibers of their lifted convex hull. The three cylindrical caps $-x-y\ge0$, $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$ cover the whole space and are each essential on this source. The endpoint areas are $w=103/200$, the middle area is $W=13/20$, and $M=42/25$. Each cap has raw mass $6811/8910$, a fraction $4865/10692<1/2$ of $M$.

If positive radial factors $r_-,r_0,r_+$ about zero with $|r_i-1|<1/10$ give an actual convexly compatible array, do not decrease $M$, and do not increase any of the three fixed cap masses, then all three factors equal one. For volume-coordinate variations the active support row $a=(-1/3,2/3,-1/3)$ and any cap row $c=(wf,Wf_0,wf)$ with $f=400/891$ and $f_0=46/99$ obey $a=(142560/1339)c-(194600/4017)(w,W,w)$. Also the original point at base zero and continuous origin has normalized depth at least $233/756>2/9$.
title: A minimal small-cap cover can block every nearby radial improvement
